clue.text: All the press reports Conservative too old?

parts.note: someone overage is past the permitted age, so too old

explanation.surface: A worry that the Tory party is too elderly, as reflected across the newspapers.
explanation.definitionFit: Coverage is the total reporting a story gets in the media, i.e. all the press reports on it.

clue.text: Discussion with girlfriend, perhaps about English book

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word for the girlfriend wraps the other letters

parts.note: a girlfriend is one example of a date, someone you go out with

explanation.surface: A talk with one's girlfriend concerning an English book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' places E and B inside DATE, giving D-EB-ATE.
explanation.definitionFit: A debate is a formal discussion or argument in which views are exchanged.

clue.text: Very fine hotel supported by British Airways?

indicators.note: in a down answer, a piece supported by another sits above it, so the hotel letter comes first

parts.note: H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet
British Airways is an example of an airline, hence the question mark

explanation.surface: A very fine hotel whose business is propped up by the national carrier.
explanation.definitionFit: A hairline crack or margin is extremely thin or fine, as thin as a hair.

clue.text: Bird, female bird

parts.note: an owl is a bird

explanation.surface: A bird, specifically a female bird.
explanation.definitionFit: Fowl is a general word for a bird, especially a domestic one such as a chicken.

clue.text: Is able to copy small snack

parts.note: to be able to do something is to say one can
to ape is to copy or mimic

explanation.surface: Someone capable of reproducing a little appetiser.
explanation.definitionFit: A canapé is a small savoury snack, typically a cracker or bread topped with something, served with drinks.

clue.text: Bill used regularly to be sad

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter of the words Bill used, starting with the first

explanation.surface: A man called Bill who was in the habit of being unhappy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'used' looks like part of the surface's past habit, but it supplies letters along with Bill.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling blue is an idiom for feeling down or melancholy.

clue.text: Secret language of fish — English?

parts.note: a cod is a fish

explanation.surface: Asking whether fish communicate in English, as some secret tongue.
explanation.definitionFit: A code is a system of words or symbols used to keep messages secret.

clue.text: Unethically taking a medicine initially by mouth

indicators.note: initially means only the opening letter of the word medicine is used

parts.note: medicine taken by mouth is taken orally

explanation.surface: Someone behaving badly by swallowing a dose of medicine.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting amorally means acting without regard to morality, which is acting without ethics.

clue.text: Fix up couple again

parts.note: RE is the prefix meaning again, as in redo
a pair is a couple

explanation.surface: Setting up two people once more as a couple.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests matchmaking; read RE-PAIR, pairing again.
explanation.definitionFit: To fix up something broken is to mend or restore it.

clue.text: Dull field study

parts.note: a lea is a meadow or field, a poetic word
a den is a private room for study or work

explanation.surface: A boring piece of research into a field.
explanation.definitionFit: Leaden, literally heavy as lead, figuratively means dull, sluggish or lifeless.

clue.text: Roman sea horse

definitions.meaning: in Latin, the language of the Romans

explanation.surface: A seahorse from ancient Rome.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin mare means sea, and in English a mare is an adult female horse.

clue.text: Where batter needs to stand to rise

definitions.meaning: in cricket the batter stands in the crease, the line-marked area by the stumps, to be safe from being run out or stumped
to rise is to grow or go up in amount

explanation.surface: Instructions on where the cake batter should be left to rise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'batter' suggests baking, with 'rise' to match, but it is the cricketer; in cricket the crease is the marked line at each end of the pitch.
explanation.definitionFit: Increase as a verb means to grow larger or go up, as prices rise.

clue.text: Just after money for expensive fabric

indicators.note: after means the word for just is placed following the word for money

parts.note: cash is money
mere means just, as in a mere child

explanation.surface: Someone who is only interested in money buying costly cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: Cashmere is a fine, soft and costly wool from Kashmir goats.

clue.text: Spies finally remove surveillance

indicators.note: finally means only the last letter of the word Spies is used

parts.note: to take out something is to remove it

explanation.surface: Spies at last withdrawing their monitoring.
explanation.definitionFit: A stakeout is a period of covert watching of a place or person by police or agents.

clue.text: Uncalled for to provoke Nazi police

parts.note: to needle someone is to provoke or irritate them
the SS was the Nazi paramilitary police force

explanation.surface: It was pointless to antagonise the Nazi security forces.
explanation.definitionFit: Something needless is unnecessary, and so uncalled for.

clue.text: Error removed from V-1 missile sketch

indicators.note: removed from means the error word is taken out of the missile's name

parts.note: the doodlebug was the British wartime nickname for the German V-1 flying bomb
a bug is an error, especially in software

explanation.surface: A fault eliminated from the design drawing of a wartime rocket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'removed from' takes BUG off the end of DOODLEBUG, leaving the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A doodle is an idle, aimless sketch or scribble.

clue.text: Bivalve left in river

indicators.note: in means the letter for left goes inside the river's name

parts.note: the Cam is the river that flows through Cambridge

explanation.surface: A shellfish abandoned in a river.
explanation.definitionFit: A clam is a bivalve mollusc, a shellfish with two hinged shells.

clue.text: Dead body of rook in a group of trees

indicators.note: in means the rook's letter goes inside the word for the trees

parts.note: a copse is a small group of trees
R is the chess notation for a rook

explanation.surface: The carcass of a rook found lying in a small wood.
explanation.definitionFit: A corpse is a dead body, usually a human one.

clue.text: Go along with sector changes

indicators.note: changes signals that the letters of sector are rearranged

explanation.surface: Accept the changes being made to a sector.
explanation.definitionFit: To escort someone is to accompany them, going along with them.

clue.text: Oven-cooked dish starts to smoke the embarrassing way

indicators.note: starts to means taking the opening letter of each of the following words

explanation.surface: A casserole that begins to give off smoke, to the cook's shame.
explanation.definitionFit: A stew is a dish of meat and vegetables slowly cooked in liquid, often in the oven.

clue.text: Some unfortunate fish

indicators.note: some means only part of the word unfortunate is taken, the letters sitting within it

explanation.surface: Some fish that have had bad luck.
explanation.definitionFit: Tuna is a large ocean fish, also eaten tinned or as steaks.

clue.text: Noticed big ship in Mediterranean

indicators.note: in means the ship goes inside the short name for the sea

parts.note: the Med is the usual short name for the Mediterranean
Noah's ark was a big ship

explanation.surface: A large vessel spotted in the Mediterranean.
explanation.definitionFit: Marked as a verb means noted or paid attention to, as in marked my words.

clue.text: Concerned with large ship round cape that goes flat out

indicators.note: round means the two words together surround the cape letter

parts.note: re means concerning or about, as in business letters
a liner is a large passenger ship
C is the abbreviation for cape on maps

explanation.surface: A big ship sailing round a headland at full speed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flat out' suggests top speed, but here it means lying flat.
explanation.definitionFit: A recliner is a chair whose back tips back so the sitter can lie almost flat.

clue.text: Endlessly examine horses at breeding farm

indicators.note: endlessly means the last letter of the word for examine is dropped

parts.note: to study something is to examine it closely

explanation.surface: Inspecting the horses at a breeding farm without end.
explanation.definitionFit: A stud is an establishment where horses are kept for breeding, or the horses kept there.
